Issue 1 (System Log tab freeze) — DIAGNOSED + FIXED (t1). Please queue QA review (t4).

ROOT CAUSE (empirically confirmed, not code-reading):
The ~3-5s GUI freeze was NOT the System Log tab's rendering (that's only ~75-200ms with the inline throttle/cap/setUpdatesEnabled fixes). It was a BLOCKING MCP call running on the GUI main thread.

- gui_tab_onboarding.py:673 `refresh_from_state()` → `_refresh_symbols()` → `bridge.fetch_symbol_prices()` (gui_bridge.py:349) → `exec_layer.get_symbols()` → `_ensure_session()`. `_ensure_session` retries a failed/never-connected MCP session with a 2s `time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY)` (execution_layer_v2.py:376). With MCP unreachable/slow, each call blocks ~2s.
- `_on_poll` (gui_main.py) runs every 1s and calls the CURRENT tab's `refresh_from_state()`. While the Onboarding tab (index 0) is current, every poll blocked ~2s. Measured: `MainWindow._on_poll took 2023 ms (curtab=0)` — the whole GUI froze ~2s/1s (appears as persistent 3-5s freeze).
- Switching to System Log itself is fast (no block; SystemLogTab.refresh_from_state() is a no-op), but the user could barely reach it while the onboarding tab was freezing the whole UI. So the reported "System Log tab freeze" is really the global GUI-thread block.

FIX (2 files):
1. gui_bridge.py — made `SystemBridge.fetch_symbol_prices()` NON-BLOCKING: it now returns a thread-safe snapshot of a `_price_cache` (dict, lock-protected) that the background MCP refresh daemon thread (`refresh_state_from_mcp`) populates via a new `_fetch_prices_blocking()` helper. GUI thread never calls MCP from this path. (Verified thread-safe: returns a copy; mutating the snapshot doesn't corrupt the cache.)
2. gui_tab_system_log.py — added `showEvent`/`hideEvent` so the 1.5s rebuild QTimer pauses while the tab is hidden (no more rebuilding a hidden table on the GUI thread) and refreshes immediately on activation.

VERIFICATION (offscreen GUI + faulthandler + instrumentation):
- Before: `MainWindow._on_poll took 2023 ms (curtab=0)`; main-thread faulthandler stack stuck in `_ensure_session`/`fetch_symbol_prices` for seconds.
- After: `_on_poll took 53 ms`; main thread idle at `app.exec()` during event loop; only background daemon threads (mcp-refresh loop, position-poll loop) are in `_ensure_session`, which is correct. Switching to System Log tab = ~250-310ms (includes fresh-data refresh), no MCP block.
- Smoke test cycling all 5 tabs: no exceptions; tab times 0-250ms.
- AST parse OK on both files.

Task t2 (Issue 2 — Live Control Send Order) DONE. Root cause found + fixed, verified empirically against a faithful mock MT5 MCP server.

ROOT CAUSE (definitive, reproducible): ExecutionLayer.send_order read success/retcode/price directly off the raw MCP tool-result envelope {"content":[{"text":"<json>"}]} without unwrapping it. get_account_info/get_symbols/get_new_candles already call the existing _parse_mcp_response() helper, but send_order/close_position/get_positions did not. Result: order_result.get("success")->None and retcode check ->False, so EVERY order was misclassified as failed with "Unknown error" even when MT5 filled (retcode 10009). This is why the manual Send Order appeared to "not work" — the GUI always wrote "Order FAILED ... Unknown error", never registering a real fill. It is NOT a price/order_type rejection bug; the order was actually being sent and filled.

PROOF (mock wraps all results in the MCP content envelope like the real bridge): exact payload sent = {"symbol":"XAUUSD","volume":0.43,"order_type":0,"price":2650.5,"sl":2648.2,"tp":2655.0,"comment":"LSW-V2-<eid>","magic":20791}. BEFORE: success=false "Unknown error"; AFTER: success=true/order_sent=true/retcode=10009/filled 2650.55.

CONTRACT ANSWERS: order_type = int 0/1 (0=buy,1=sell), accepted; price is passed but fill uses current market, a stale/far price triggers a rejection which the code now surfaces (proved retcode 10015 "Invalid price..." surfaced, not "Unknown error"); risk-based lot 0.43 IS accepted (not a 0.01 fallback); required fields symbol/volume/order_type/price/sl/tp/comment/magic all sent.

FIX: trading_live/live/engine/execution_layer_v2.py only — added _parse_mcp_response() unwrap in send_order, close_position, get_positions. Backward-compatible (returns dict unchanged if no "content"). NO GUI logic changed. Compile + import verify commands both pass (ORDER_COMPILE_OK / ORDER_IMPORT_OK).

RESIDUAL: could not authenticate to the real MT5 MCP (port 22346 -> 401; no MCP_TOKEN found via env/state/DB/config grep), so the contract was validated against a faithful mock; price/order_type should be spot-checked against the real server once a token is set. The envelope-parsing bug is self-contained and is the actual cause. Ready for QA review (t5).

UPDATE to my Issue 1 (t1) fix — final state corrected after further empirical verification:

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): ~3-5s GUI freeze was a BLOCKING MCP call on the GUI main thread.
- gui_tab_onboarding.py:673 refresh_from_state() → bridge.fetch_symbol_prices() (gui_bridge.py:349) → exec_layer.get_symbols() → _ensure_session() (execution_layer_v2.py:376) retries a failed MCP session with a 2s `time.sleep`. _on_poll (gui_main.py) runs every 1s and calls the CURRENT tab's refresh_from_state(); while onboarding (index 0) is current, EVERY poll blocked ~2s → whole GUI frozen ~2s/1s (perceived 3-5s). Measured `MainWindow._on_poll took 2023 ms (curtab=0)`.

A SECOND residual stall (caught by faulthandler): SystemLogTab `_refresh_log` → `_populate_table` rebuilt the ENTIRE up-to-2000-row table every tick when new entries arrived (~500ms under GIL contention, >0.5s acceptance). The initial `_load_from_db` pre-fills the buffer to 2000, so every refresh overflows → full rebuild.

FIX (2 files, confined to inScope):
1. live/gui/gui_bridge.py — fetch_symbol_prices() is now NON-BLOCKING: reads a thread-safe _price_cache (populated on the bg MCP-refresh daemon thread via new _fetch_prices_blocking()/ _publish_price_cache() in refresh_state_from_mcp). GUI thread never calls MCP from this path.
2. live/gui/gui_tab_system_log.py — _refresh_log now does a DIFF-BASED sliding-window update: it snapshots the old visible rows, trims/appends _all_entries, diffs by id, then only removes the front rows that fell out of the window and appends the new rows (_apply_incremental + _set_cell_items helper). Per-tick cost is O(#new+#dropped) instead of O(rows). (I initially tried showEvent/hideEvent but that caused a re-entrant _populate_table hang during tab switch — REVERTED.)

VERIFIED (offscreen + faulthandler, contract verify commands both pass):
- Before: _on_poll=2023ms, main thread stuck in _ensure_session/fetch_symbol_prices for seconds.
- After: _on_poll=53ms; freeze_repro.py exits 0 — "PASS: main thread stayed in Qt event loop (no block >0.5s) for 6.52s after switching to System Log; switch=106.4ms". py_compile COMPILE_OK. SystemLogTab populates 1867 rows / buffer 2000, timer active.
- No change to execution_layer_v2.py (Issue 2 scope) or gui_main.py.

NOTES for coordination (not blockers): the same _ensure_session 2s retry sleep affects other GUI-triggered MCP calls (Account connect, Live Control send order) — likely relevant to Issues 2/3.
